1.why: All seven screens are static with no animations, carousels or pop-up dialogs; only the technical 'Logs' panel with a 64-character token adds some visual noise to an otherwise calm layout.

2.why: Bold step headings, green status banners and one blue primary button do stand out, but the 'Your steps' progress list renders as run-together text ('1. 1. Request2. 2. Confirm code') and the acceptance checkbox in Step 6 is tiny and visually collided with the button.

3.why: Each screen shows only one form and one action so the next task is easy to spot, yet the required recovery token and safety code must be hunted for in the technical Logs box at the bottom of the page.

4.why: The persistent 6-step list and 'what to do next' banners reduce load, but she still must transcribe a 64-character token, a six-digit code and satisfy a four-part password rule stated only as prose.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, autofill hint, password-manager suggestion or even a show-password toggle appears on any screen, including the sign-in step.

6.why: Nothing familiar is presented back to her — no pre-filled/masked email, no saved account tile or device recognition; only static field labels are repeated.

7.why: Sentences are short, plain and in a large readable font ('Use your new password to securely sign in.'), though the garbled step-list line is hard to read.

8.why: No error or validation message is visible in any of the seven screenshots, so the claim that errors explain the problem and the fix cannot be confirmed for this system.

9.why: There are no placeholder examples or sample formats for the email, the 64-character token, the six-digit code or the password — only rule descriptions in text.

10.why: The single password-plus-code path is clearly labelled at each step ('Recovery token', 'Safety code', 'Password'), although no alternative methods such as face login exist to choose between.

11.why: Every screen offers exactly one input area and one primary button, so she is never faced with competing options.

12.why: Each step opens with an explicit green outcome banner ('Code confirmed…', 'Your password has been changed…', 'Privacy conditions accepted…') and the Logs list confirms completed actions.

13.why: A persistent 'Need help?' card plus a one-line instruction under each step heading provide tips ('Enter the six-digit safety code from Logs.'), though there is no contact route or per-field help link.

14.why: No back link, 'resend code', 'start over' or edit affordance is visible anywhere, and the log states the reset token is now single-use, so recovering from a mistake is not shown as easy.

15.why: All seven screens reuse the same header, step tracker, card layout, blue button style and help/logs panels in identical positions.
